texts.facts: 1. In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 13.05.2019 at about 03.20 hour, petitioner was going on his cycle to his residence. When he reached at Okhla Cantt. Bust Stop, Harkesh Nagar, New Delhi and he was standing at the side of the road / footpath then in the meanwhile, one vehicle bearing no. Innova Car bearing no. DL 3CBD 4990 came at a fast speed in a rash and negligent manner and hit the petitioner with a great force and due to such impact petitioner fell on the road along with his cycle and sustained grievous injuries. 3. It is further stated that after the accident someone called at 100 number for PCR and after some time PCR van came and took injured to Trauma Center, AIIMS where his MLC was prepared. 4. Further the FIR in question was registered and ultimately charge sheet u/s 279/338 IPC was filed in the present case. Page No. 2 of 24 RP 5. Further, Medical Board of Pt. Madan Mohan Hospital, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi sent disability report dated 07.05.2021 noticing 03% permanent physical impairment in relation to his left lower limb. 6. In response to petition, as per record driver / R-1 and owner R-2 appeared and filed their reply. 7. In nutshell, it is stated by R-1 & 2 that no accident took place by the alleged offending vehicle in question by the negligence of R-1. It is further stated that R-1 was driving the vehicle carefully in normal speed and due to fault of petitioner himself, accident in question took place. It is further claimed that vehicle of the R-1 & 2 is wrongly involved in connivance of local police just to get the compensation from insurance company. It is further stated that vehicle of the R-1 & 2 was fully insured by R-3 at the time of accident. It is further claimed that R-1/ driver was having a valid driving license at the time of accident. Copy of the same is placed on record. As such, they stated that claim, if any is payable by the insurance company only. 8. In reply filed by insurance company/ R-3 in nutshell it is stated that R-1 was driving the offending vehicle in question in violation of provision of motor vehicle Act and was not holding a valid driving license at the time of accident. It is further stated that as per the DL verification conducted by R-3/ insurance company, from RTO, Ambala, Haryanal, the DL of R-1 was valid upto 25.03.2019, LMV non transport vehicles and thereafter the same was renewed only on 17.06.2019 where as the date of accident is 13.05.2019. Thus, MACT No.: 732/19 Suraj Yadav Vs. Amarjeet & Ors. Page No. 3 of 24 RP at the time of accident there was no valid DL as even grace period of one month for renewal of DL as already expired in April, 2019. As such, it is further claimed by insurance company that R-3 is not liable to indemnify the insured R/-2 in the present case. It is further stated that R-2 entrusted Suraj Yadav vs . Amarjeet & Ors. on 14 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153878629/ 2 the offending vehicle to R-1 willingly but illegally although, such R-1 did not had any valid driving license and same is in violation of Sect. 149 (2) of MV Act. It is further stated that as such no legal offer is made in the present case to settle the claim. 9. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 13.12.2019 by Predecessor of this Tribunal: 1. As per record, Petitioner examined himself only, as PW-1. Such PW-1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents including the discharge summary and medical bills, Ex. PW- 1/1 to Ex. PW-1/9. He was cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company/R-3 as well as by learned counsel for R-1/driver and R-2/ owner. Further, as per record, R-1 & R-2 did not lead any evidence. 13. But R-3/ insurance company examined R3W1, Amit Kumar from their office on the aspect of validity of DL in question. 17. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The Rs. 15,000/- petitioner has not filed any bill for conveyance. The nature of injuries are grievous and petitioner suffered 3% permanent physical impairment in relation to his left lower limb.

Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 22. The following observation of the High Court of Australia in Astley v. Austrust Ltd.1 is worthy of quoting: "A finding of contributory negligence turns on a factual investi- gation whether the plaintiff contributed to his or her own loss by failing to take reasonable care of his or her person or property. What is reasonable care depends on the circumstances of the case. In many cases, it may be proper for a plaintiff to rely on the defendant to perform its duty. But there is no abso-lute rule. In some cases, the nature of the duty MACT No.: 732/19 Suraj Yadav Vs. Amarjeet & Ors. Page No. 7 of 24 RP owed may exculpate the plaintiff from a claim of con-tributory negligence; in other cases, the nature of the duty may reduce the plaintiffs share of responsibility for the damage suffered; and in yet other cases the nature of the duty may not prevent a finding that the plaintiff failed to take reasonable care for the safety of his or her person or property. Contribu-tory negligence focuses on the conduct of the plaintiff. The duty owed by the defendant, although relevant, is one only of many factors that must be weighed in determining whether the plaintiff has so conducted itself that it failed to take reasonable care for the safety of its person or property." Page No. 8 of 24 RP judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. Swaran Singh ((2004) 3SCC 297)", the compensation will be payable in the first instance by the insurance company, but with liberty to recover the same from the R-1 & 2. 37. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. 41. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of illiterate claimants, the Tribunal is allowed to consider the request for lumpsum payment for effecting purchase of any movable property such as agricultural implements, rickshaws etc. to earn a living. But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the MACT No.: 732/19 Suraj Yadav Vs. Amarjeet & Ors. Page No. 19 of 24 RP amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid.
